solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get the better of, where love is involved?

definitions.text: Get the better of, where love is involved

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up inside something else, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to best someone is to get the better of them
love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about winning over someone when romance is at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: BEST with O inside gives BESOT, and to besot someone is to overcome their judgement, typically with love.
explanation.definitionFit: To besot is to infatuate, making someone foolishly overcome, which is getting the better of them through love.

clue.text: I've strings, offering various introductions to Brad and Angelina Jolie

indicators.note: introductions are opening parts, and various says they are of differing lengths

parts.note: the opening letter of the first name
the opening two letters of the second name
the opening two letters of the surname

explanation.surface: A stringed instrument boasting that it introduced a famous Hollywood couple to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written in the instrument's own voice. The openings taken are one, two and two letters long, which is what 'various' warns of.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument, so it could say of itself that it has strings.

clue.text: Trebles I placed under of training of parson

indicators.note: in a down entry, placed under means the piece sits below, so it comes last
training puts something through drills and reshapes it, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choirmaster's note: the boy trebles are placed under a parson's training.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed Observer clue has a single 'of' ('placed under training of parson'); the online copy's extra 'of' is a slip and does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: Soprani is the Italian plural of soprano, and trebles are boy sopranos, the highest voices in a choir.

clue.text: Dislodges judge removed from top of lists

indicators.note: removed from the top means the opening letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: the lists were the arena for tilting, so by extension the tournaments held there
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A judge has been struck off the top of the rankings and loses position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lists' looks like rankings, but it is the medieval jousting ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to drive them out of a place or position, the same as dislodging them.

clue.text: Cartel administered with energy and cajolery

indicators.note: administered means dealt out or managed, so the letters are handled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A business cartel run with vigour and a good deal of sweet talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The energy letter joins the shuffle with the six letters of the business word.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is used figuratively for cloying, sugary flattery, the kind of wheedling talk that is cajolery.

clue.text: Ambitious climber, not on watch, about to freeze

indicators.note: about means around, so the earlier pieces wrap round the last one

parts.note: a switch that is not on is off
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover over its face
to ice something is to freeze it

explanation.surface: A mountaineer about to freeze on the slope while off his guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The two outer pieces wrap round the middle one. 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a social climber; a hunter is a watch with a protective lid.
explanation.definitionFit: An office-hunter is someone who seeks public office for its rewards, an ambitious careerist or social climber.

clue.text: Like a strong gale, we'll be caught in turns with those at sea

indicators.note: being caught in means trapped inside, so the short word sits in the middle of the rearranged letters
at sea means confused or adrift, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
taken as written, as letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors warned that a strong gale will catch them as they make turns at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou'wester is a strong gale from the southwest, so such a gale is southwestern.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong gale blowing from the southwest, the prevailing stormy quarter in Britain, is described as southwestern.

clue.text: Trouble for the Scots mainly, undoing trust

indicators.note: undoing something takes it apart, so these letters are pulled out of their order and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Breaking someone's trust brings trouble, and a Scot would have a word for it.
explanation.walkthrough: STURT is a chiefly Scottish word, which is why the definition says 'for the Scots mainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturt is a Scots and northern dialect noun for strife, vexation or bother.

clue.text: Painter Italy once rejected, a colossus

indicators.note: rejected once means thrown out a single time, so only one of the matching letters goes

parts.note: the Venetian Renaissance painter
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian painter of colossal reputation, once spurned by his own country.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter's name has two of the letter for Italy, and 'once' says only one is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giant gods of Greek myth, so a titan is any person or thing of colossal size or power.

clue.text: Noodle, one that cook's captivated by

indicators.note: being captivated by something means being held captive inside it

parts.note: un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good un'
to do food is to cook it, as in doing the potatoes

explanation.surface: A single noodle that has charmed the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noodle' could be a silly person; here it is the Japanese food.
explanation.definitionFit: Udon is a thick Japanese wheat noodle, so one strand or serving is a noodle.

clue.text: Rachmanite, wretch trapping tiresome fool, see, had up

definitions.note: Rachmanite names a person, and Chambers allows the noun rack-rent for one who charges such rent, short for rack-renter

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the first word goes round the reversed pieces

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible wretch

indicators.note: in a down entry, having something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nerk is British slang for an irritating idiot
the letter C sounds like see

explanation.surface: An exploitative landlord, a wretch who has a tiresome idiot arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Rachman was a notorious 1950s London slum landlord who charged extortionate rents; 'had up' suggests an arrest but reverses the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rachmanite is an exploitative landlord like Rachman, someone charging an excessive, extortionate rent for property.

clue.text: Sweet wine: see message on gift to Katharine?

parts.note: describes what the following words form: a gift tag
taken as written
Kay is a pet form of the name Katharine

explanation.surface: A bottle of dessert wine with a gift tag for Katharine.
explanation.walkthrough: A gift tag reads 'To' and the recipient's name, so the message would be TO KAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet dessert wine from the Tokaj region of Hungary.

clue.text: Grande passion, a trap for Jock with four involved (8, two words)

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a trap with something in it holds that thing, so the twisted letters sit inside the mouth

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth, and MOU is the Scots word for mouth; Jock stands for a Scot

indicators.note: involved can mean tangled or convoluted, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A grand romance described as something a Scotsman could be caught up in four times over.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman, so 'for Jock' asks for a Scots word: MOU, the mouth or trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour fou is French for mad, obsessive love, the sort of grand passion the French phrase grande passion also names.

clue.text: What'll make you go dizzy, knocked back?

definitions.text: What'll make you go dizzy, knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a spin round and round makes you giddy

explanation.surface: A riddle about what makes your head swim when you knock it back.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: SPIN reversed is NIPS, and nips of spirits, knocked back as drinks, will make you dizzy too.
explanation.definitionFit: Nips are small measures of spirits, and swallowing several quickly (knocking them back) makes a drinker light-headed.

clue.text: Ship's timber, fine bottom but not bow

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: but not says the following letter must be left out of the word before

parts.note: a buttock is one half of the bottom
B is a recognised abbreviation for bow

explanation.surface: Describing a vessel: fine at the stern but not at the prow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like the front of the ship in the surface, but it only stands for the letter B to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A futtock is one of the curved timbers that make up the ribs of a wooden ship's frame.

clue.text: Drink cheers islander's beloved

parts.note: a jar is a British slang word for a drink, especially of beer
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: Raising a glass with a toast to a loved one on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The islander is a Shetlander: JARTA is a Shetland term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Jarta is a Shetland dialect word for a dear or darling, used to address a loved one.

clue.text: Boat people identifiable by a few short lines?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a community in southern China who traditionally live on boats
second meaning: a Japanese verse form of five short lines

explanation.surface: A question about whether a seafaring community can be recognised by brief lines of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links the two meanings with 'identifiable by', but they are unrelated senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tanka are a boat-dwelling people of the Guangdong coast, and a tanka is a five-line Japanese poem of 31 syllables.

clue.text: Wife of prince he shuts in most of zenana with one

indicators.note: shutting something in encloses it, so the first word goes around the next piece

parts.note: he refers to a male, a man

indicators.note: most of means all but the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a zenana is the women's quarters of a house in South Asia, and a haram is the same thing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Indian prince confines his wife to the women's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Haram is a variant spelling of harem, the secluded women's quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharani is the wife or widow of a maharaja, an Indian prince.

clue.text: Chapel: see one go here after church

indicators.note: after places the pieces named before it behind the piece named after it

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Directions to a chapel: someone may have a go here after attending church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a bishop's see, which fits a chapel, but it only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chantry is a chapel endowed for the saying of masses for the soul of its founder.

clue.text: College swat learned laboriously — such a one?

definitions.text: College swat learned laboriously — such a one

indicators.note: laboriously suggests hard work and effort, so the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for college
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A student at college who mugs up hard, and the clue asks what to call such a person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: a swot who studies late into the night burns candles, and so is a candle-waster.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle-waster is one who studies or carouses late into the night, burning candles in the process.

clue.text: See carpet in hall for what's spilt from salad bowl?

indicators.note: in places the floor covering inside the word for a hall

parts.note: an aula is a hall, from the Latin
a rug is a small carpet

explanation.surface: Look at the stains on the hall carpet where the salad bowl was knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: A salad green is what falls out when a salad bowl is spilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Arugula is the American name for rocket, a peppery leaf served in salads.

clue.text: Girl turned up in hat for husbandry

indicators.note: in places the flipped word inside the headwear

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up flips the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A girl turns up in a hat looking for a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husbandry' looks like a hunt for a husband, but it is farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the cultivation of land for crops, a branch of husbandry or farming.

clue.text: A little bit astray, he's inside — one won't be cured (12, two words)

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount

indicators.note: inside says the short word goes into the middle of the longer assembly

parts.note: erring is going astray
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man wandering slightly astray and ending up in jail who is beyond reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's inside' looks like someone in prison, and 'won't be cured' like an incorrigible case; cured here means smoked or salted.
explanation.definitionFit: A white herring is a fresh one, as opposed to a red herring that has been cured by salting and smoking.

clue.text: Common time in composer, American, one associated with merrymaking

indicators.note: in places the musical time signature inside the name of the composer

parts.note: J S Bach, the German composer
common time, four beats in a bar, is written as a C on the stave
US is short for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A musical note about time signatures in a composer's work, plus an American revel.
explanation.walkthrough: Common time is the 4/4 time signature, marked with a C symbol in printed music.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine and revelry, the figure most associated with drunken merrymaking.

clue.text: What'll distinguish a woman abroad? For example being wrapped in sponge

indicators.note: being wrapped in means enclosed by, so the short abbreviation sits inside the other word

parts.note: to bum is to sponge off others, to cadge
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how to tell a woman apart when overseas, for instance by a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a title: in South Asia a Muslim lady of rank is distinguished by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Begum is a title of respect given to a Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia, distinguishing her socially.

clue.text: Source of vegetable oil, unknown in soft drink

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the name of the drink

parts.note: cola is a fizzy soft drink
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A mystery ingredient in a soft drink turns out to be plant oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The algebra convention makes z one of the letters used for an unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Colza is rapeseed, whose seeds are pressed to yield colza oil, a vegetable oil.

clue.text: See one who wrote poetically of love, what few will have avoided

parts.note: the letter C sounds like see

parts.words: one who wrote poetically of love
parts.note: the Roman poet whose works include the Amores and the Art of Love

explanation.surface: An instruction to read a classical love poet, followed by something almost nobody escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the pandemic illness that almost everyone caught at some point.
explanation.definitionFit: Covid-19 spread so widely during the pandemic that very few people managed to avoid catching it.

clue.text: Decorate with stones giving distinguished Turk a dash

parts.note: beg is a variant of bey, a title for a Turkish governor or man of rank
an em dash is a long dash in printing, named for its width

explanation.surface: A distinguished Turkish gentleman given a dashing jewelled decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: An em is a printer's measure, and an em dash is the long dash.
explanation.definitionFit: To begem is to adorn or set with gems, that is to decorate with precious stones.

clue.text: Business, one that's died, parts reallocated

indicators.note: reallocating the parts moves the end portion of the word round to its front

parts.note: a goner is someone who is dead or done for

explanation.surface: A firm whose one key figure has died and whose divisions are being redistributed.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word after its third letter and swap the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergon is Greek for work, used in English for business or a task undertaken.

clue.text: Depression that's unavoidable in singleness

indicators.note: something unavoidable in a word is bound to be found within it

parts.note: the letters run consecutively in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: Low spirits that come inevitably with being single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like gloom, but it is a hollow in the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, a depression in the land between hills, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Grand jug, feature of crest, purple

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
an olpe is an ancient Greek jug

explanation.surface: A grand jug decorated in purple with a crest on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The crest is heraldic, and the definition names both what the thing is and its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a golpe is a purple roundel, a disc that can appear on a coat of arms or crest.

clue.text: Salt mostly delayed, caught in storm

indicators.note: caught in says one piece is trapped inside another

parts.note: a gale is a storm wind

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: delayed is late

explanation.surface: A shipment of salt that has mostly been held up by a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is the chemical sense, a compound formed from an acid.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallate is a salt or ester of gallic acid, a chemical compound found in gall-nuts.

clue.text: Guy, last of gang trailing those in front

indicators.note: trailing puts the piece behind, following the other piece

parts.note: the van is the front of an army or procession

indicators.note: last of keeps only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of gang

explanation.surface: A man at the back of a gang following its leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man; it is a guy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A vang is a rope or tackle on a sailing boat that steadies the gaff, a kind of guy rope.

clue.text: I got 'gutted' in drunken revel, being a liberal-minded person

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, so the word keeps only its outer letters
in places the first pieces inside the reworked letters
drunken suggests reeling about, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
taken as written
got with its middle letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being thoroughly drunk at a party, yet claims to be an open-minded liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an Afrikaans word, from South African politics of the apartheid era.
explanation.definitionFit: A verligte was an enlightened, progressive Afrikaner, as opposed to a verkrampte, a hardline conservative.

clue.text: Tower, a feature of museum in Arabia

indicators.note: a feature of something forms part of it, so the letters lie within the following words

parts.note: the letters run consecutively across these words

explanation.surface: A tower forms part of a museum in Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of museum, all of in, and the start of Arabia join up.
explanation.definitionFit: A minar is a tower or turret, especially a lighthouse or a minaret in Islamic architecture.

clue.text: Cancel from bequest a reward reversed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reversed says the word just before is written from its last letter to its first

parts.note: meed is an old word for a reward

explanation.surface: A legacy withdrawn, as a reward turned back.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the reward is turned round; the A stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To adeem is a legal term for revoking a legacy, when the item bequeathed no longer exists in the estate.
